keyset_id_finding.summary: cdk writes SHORT keyset ids in both token formats: V4 at the token level (8 bytes) and V3 per proof (16 hex). Every consumer must resolve short ids against the mint's keyset list; every mint in the cdk family natively resolves them.

evidence.target: CBOR decode of the committed V4 fixture + JSON decode of all V3 fixtures
evidence.observed: V4 t[0].i = 8 bytes 01e73e75a0809604; every V3 proof id = the same 16-hex value; the mint's canonical keyset id is the 33-byte form

evidence.location: crates/cashu/src/nuts/nut00/mod.rs:519 (ProofV3.keyset_id: ShortKeysetId), crates/cashu/src/nuts/nut02.rs:383 (ShortKeysetId: v1 = whole id, v2 = 8-byte prefix)

keyset_id_finding.retraction: The earlier v0-era narrative — that the 16-hex spelling was a test minter's 'v2-short truncation' transplanted from V4 (PRTA#247) — is RETRACTED: the short spelling is cdk's native V3 output, byte-identical across the 'valid' and so-called 'truncated' fixtures. The portal@pin defect was short-id resolution, not malformed tokens.
